name: Kyrgyz Republic
headline: Kyrgyz Republic: +11.1% growth in 2025, 8.2% inflation, debt 39% of GDP
sections: Kyrgyz Republic is a $22.6 billion economy (2025), the world's 129th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +11.1% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $9,220 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 13.7% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 8.2% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 13.9% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 4.0% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 8.2% (2025).
Gross government debt is 39% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 64% in 2020. The general government balance is +2.6% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is −24.9% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 92% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.8% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 31% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 72.4 years (2024). Population: 7.2 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
